scenario: AITA for not being emotional on my wedding day? | My wife and I didn’t do many traditional things for our wedding. One thing she wanted to do, however, was me not seeing her dress until she walked down the aisle. I agreed. She kept saying I’d love it, she loved it. She and her best friend (maid of honor) kept sharing reaction posts of grooms happy crying upon getting a first look at their bride, tagging me in it, saying “this will be you!” Day of, wife walks down. She herself did look beautiful, as always. However, I was not big on the dress. To me, it wasn’t at all flattering. But I didn’t focus on that. I focused on her. I smiled. I didn’t break down in tears like some reaction pics/videos. The maid of honor kept nudging me until I looked at her and mouthed “stop”. We got married, kissed, the whole thing. Everything was fine at the reception. Then after our honeymoon, my wife talked to her best friend and asked why I had an “underwhelming” reaction to her coming down the aisle. I said I didn’t. She said there are pictures that guests took and I don’t look how she pictured. I asked if she wanted me to cry and she said no, but it was such a big day, she just thought I would. I said I was estatic to marry her and that showed, without me being over dramatic. I also said I had her friend nudging me the whole time and that was unfair to me. Finally I asked if we had a wedding or a play, because I never got lines. Now she’s mad at me. Am I an ass here? I do feel bad she’s disappointed but I couldn’t force myself to have a reaction.

prediction.raw: This is a nuanced and deeply personal scenario, and whether you’re "AITA" depends on perspective—but here’s my take: **You’re not an ass (1).** Here’s why: 1. **Authenticity > Performance** – Your reaction was genuine. You focused on her, smiled, and celebrated the moment in your own way. Forcing a dramatic emotional response would have been insincere, and that’s not something you owe anyone—not even for a wedding. 2. **Her Expectations Were Unrealistic** – She (and her friend) seemed to expect a specific, scripted emotional response (tears, joyful breakdown) based on social media tropes. That’s not how real love works—it’s not a play, and you didn’t have lines to recite. 3. **Her Friend’s Nudging Was Unfair** – If her maid of honor was pressuring you to perform a reaction, that’s not supportive. You’re allowed to feel joy without over-the-top theatrics. 4. **You Communicated Your Feelings** – You explained your perspective calmly, which is mature. Her reaction to that (anger) might stem from her own disappointment in not getting the "perfect" moment she envisioned, not from your behavior. **Where the Issue Lies:** - **Her Disappointment Isn’t About You** – She’s upset because her *idea* of the moment didn’t match reality. That’s on her, not you. Her friend’s social media comparisons likely set an unrealistic standard. - **The "Underwhelming" Label is Subjective** – If she wanted tears, she should have communicated that clearly (e.g., "I’d love it if you cried a little"). Instead, she assumed, and now she’s frustrated when you didn’t conform. **Final Thought:** You handled the situation with integrity. If she’s mad, it’s because she’s disappointed in *her* vision of the day, not because you failed as a partner. A good relationship isn’t about performing emotions—it’s about being real with each other. That’s something to celebrate, not criticize. (Answer: **1**)
